key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes adapt gradient descent to local curvature, steering it toward flatter minima while preserving convergence under stated assumptions.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers an adaptive stepsize approach for seeking low-loss, low-sharpness solutions, with empirical results extending to pre-trained LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use curvature-adaptive oscillations near the minimizer manifold, with damping driving convergence.
At small loss, projected iterates approximately descend log top-Hessian-eigenvalue sharpness along the manifold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform-in-time sharpness and loss-reduction guarantees for locally quadratic Morse–Bott losses, plus SAM-like flattening in nonlinear teacher–student networks and LLM fine-tuning.
watch_item: The guarantees require locally quadratic Morse–Bott structure near the minimizer manifold; the broader neural-network results are empirical.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
